oneOf.description:
The native receipt [`Compat::report`] produced; its published shape is
[`RequirementsValue`], and the value is emitted as produced rather than
re-decoded, so a shape drift is a test failure, never a runtime trap.

The delivery-requirements document: the class, the reviews it needs and
the policy it was decided under (CAD-1946).

Activation.description:
Whether default lean classification applies, and if not, why strict
requirements are retained.

oneOf.description: A valid default-equivalent policy is in force.

The policy is custom or its provenance is unknown. The serialized
name is retained for compatibility with existing requirements readers.

A `delivery:` section exists but is not the approved one
(`delivery_unapproved`) — the legacy requirements stay.

The section is malformed with no approved policy
(`delivery_error`) — the defaults apply, legacy requirements.

DeliveryClass.description: What class the evidence places the delivery in.

oneOf.description: Activated profile, allowlisted ordinary documentation only.
Activated profile, ordinary listed paths.

Reserved: `classify` resolves sensitive conditions to `Strict` and
does not currently return this variant.

No relaxation applies: the profile is not in force, the trusted
lists are unavailable, or the diff evidence is incomplete. The
requirements are exactly the legacy ones.

DeliveryPolicy.description:
A project's delivery policy — `PROJECT.md` `delivery:` or the
defaults. [`parse`] builds it through the strict raw types and
[`DeliveryPolicy::validate`]; `serde` round-trips the validated
form (the approval payload's `delivery` key).

integration_branch.description:
CAD-1561: one extra PR target beyond the repository default
branch. `None` is omitted from the canonical JSON so existing
digests and approvals are unchanged. A non-default target is
admitted only while the exact current approved policy names it —
last-approved fallbacks (`delivery_unapproved` notes) do not.

max_revise.description: REVISE verdicts a ticket takes before the operator decides.

oversized.description: Over this a delivery cannot merge through the loop.

reviews.description: The named reviews a `risk` rule may require.

risk.description:
Risk rules: a delivery must satisfy every review `require`d by
every rule whose `when` holds. A rule with no `when` always
applies.

solo_operator.description:
Optional legacy CAD-1298 profile, retained for compatible reads.
CAD-1314 needs no profile for default lean classification. Keeping
`None` omitted preserves existing canonical digests and approvals;
requirements always use [`Resolved`], never the raw file.

DeliveryRequirementsValue.description:
Success value of `delivery.requirements.evaluate`: the requirements the
evaluator produced, beside the policy they were computed under. The value is
emitted as produced; this type publishes its shape.

policy_note.description:
`delivery_unapproved:`/`delivery_error:` when the file's section is not
the one in force.

refusal.description: Why `status=ready` would be refused; present only then.

RequirementCheck.description: One requirement and whether the target met it.

oneOf.description: The manifest's `requires.core` range against the target's version.

ok.description: Whether the target's version falls inside the range.

oneOf.description: One declared contract major list against the target's profile.

ok.description: Whether every required major is supported.

stage.description:
The target's stage for `contract`; `null` when it does not
provide it.

supported.description:
The majors the target declares for `contract`; empty when the
target does not provide it.

Requirements.description: What a delivery needs to merge, derived from the class.

browser_qa.description: A `ui/` change additionally needs a Browser QA pass.

full_checks.description:
The full PR check floor applies. `false` only for routine —
where the required base-branch checks are still all required.

operator_approval.description: An exact-head operator-connection approval is required.

policy_digest.description:
Digest of the policy the requirements were computed under —
evidence binds to it and a policy change invalidates them.

reasons.description: Machine-readable reasons: why this class, what evidence decided.

reviews.description:
Independent verdict count on the exact head: `0` only for
routine under a valid default-equivalent policy.

security_capable.description:
The combined review must be filed by a security-capable
reviewer (sensitive class).

RequirementsHost.description: The version and contracts of the target that produced a receipt.

contracts.description: The target's declared contracts, name → sorted majors.

core.description: The target's version, as it participated in precedence.

RequirementsValue.description:
Success value of `app.requirements.evaluate`: the native compatibility
receipt, typed. It is the value [`Compat::report`] produced for the
supplied target, so native and non-native hosts quote one receipt shape.

This type is the *published shape* of the receipt (the op emits the
receipt itself); `receipt_matches_the_published_shape` pins it.

**Authority**: the profile is caller data, not authenticated by this
function. `compatible: true` means "every declared requirement is met by
the exact profile supplied", never "this tenant is authorized to install".
A consumer that admits must first establish that the profile it sends is
its own current, authentic host profile, and must bind the answer to the
exact manifest bytes and profile it supplied.

`ok` here is the receipt's compatibility verdict (as in the native
receipt), not the envelope's `ok`, which only says the op ran.

checks.description:
One entry per checked requirement, in declaration order (core first,
then contracts by name).

compatible.description: Whether every declared requirement is met by the target.

contracts.description: The declared contract requirements, name → sorted majors.

core.description: The declared `requires.core` range text; `null` when absent.

declared.description: Whether the manifest declared any `needs.requires` at all.

schema.description: Receipt schema; `1` is the only version.

unmet.description:
The first unmet requirement in the native wording; `null` when
compatible. The full set is in `checks`.

Review.description: One named review a rule may require. `kind` picks the variant.

oneOf.description: An independent agent review; `focus` is one of [`FOCI`].

A GitHub App check (a bot). `mode: advisory` never blocks;
`required` blocks like an agent review.
The operator decides.

ReviewKind.description: The kind of independent review `reviews` counts toward.

oneOf.description: No review required (routine under a valid default-equivalent policy).
One combined `Review (standards+spec)` verdict.

Two verdicts — Standards and Spec/security — by distinct
reviewers.

require.description: Names in `reviews` the delivery must satisfy.

when.description:
The conditions under which the rule applies — ANY of them.
Absent: the rule always applies.

paths.description:
Repo-relative, file-level globs — the same grammar as the
`areas:` reader and `paths=` ([`crate::delivery_rules::check_path`]):
`*` and `?` match inside one segment, a `**` segment any number,
a trailing `/` everything under it. Slice 3 matches them with
`areas::matches`, so the two grammars must agree.

SoloOperatorProfile.description:
The legacy solo-operator delivery profile (CAD-1298), still readable
after CAD-1314 made the tiers default for valid default-equivalent policies.
Custom, malformed and unapproved policies retain strict requirements.
`version` is forward-proofing:
`1` is the only accepted value, an unknown one refuses the whole
section, so an older binary never silently accepts a profile shape it
does not understand.

TargetStage.description:
The stage a target declares for a contract. Closed set: an unknown stage
is a profile this core cannot evaluate and refuses.

oneOf.description: A strict validator exists; nothing executes the declaration.
A consumer renders or runs the descriptor in a sandbox.

tags.description: Sorted, de-duplicated tags; present when `tags` was given and valid.
